classification.habitat: Warm humid tropical climate with good rainfall; grown in plantations on well-drained loamy soils.
classification.distribution: Native to the Moluccas; cultivated in India in Kerala, Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris, Kanyakumari) and Karnataka.

identification.description: Dark reddish-brown nail-shaped dried flower buds with four calyx teeth and an unopened rounded corolla.
identification.whole_plant: Evergreen conical tree, 8–12 m high, with aromatic leaves and flowers in terminal clusters.
identification.stem: Straight trunk with smooth greyish bark and many ascending branches.
identification.leaf: Simple, opposite, elliptic-lanceolate, glossy, leathery, gland-dotted and aromatic when crushed.
identification.flower: Flower bud 10–17.5 mm long, dark brown, with a sub-cylindrical four-sided hypanthium exuding oil when pressed, four thick divergent sepals and an unopened ball of four imbricate petals enclosing many stamens.
identification.fruit: Fruit is a one- or two-seeded purplish berry (mother of clove).
identification_points: Nail-shaped dried flower bud, 10–17.5 mm long
Four-sided hypanthium with four spreading sepals
Ball-like unopened corolla at the top
Oil exudes when pressed with a fingernail
Strongly aromatic, pungent taste with tingling of the tongue

therapeutics.precautions: Use in the stated dose; concentrated clove oil is irritant to mucosa and skin and should be diluted. Excessive use may cause gastric irritation.
therapeutics.contraindications: Undiluted oil in children; bleeding disorders and concurrent anticoagulant therapy (eugenol inhibits platelet aggregation); caution in pregnancy beyond culinary amounts.

shlokas:
लवङ्गं देवकुसुमं श्रीसंज्ञं श्रीप्रसूनकम् ।
लवङ्गं कटुकं तिक्तं लघु नेत्रहितं हिमम् ।
दीपनं पाचनं रुच्यं कफपित्तास्रनाशकृत् ।
तृष्णां छर्दिं तथाध्मानं शूलमाशु विनाशयेत् ।
कासं श्वासञ्च हिक्काञ्च क्षयं क्षययति ध्रुवम् ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists essential oil with eugenyl acetate and caryophyllene; eugenol (about 70–85% of clove oil) gives the local anaesthetic and antiseptic action.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Clove is a powerful aromatic herb that acts as a pain reliever, especially for toothaches, and stimulates digestion.
recognized_uses: Clove oil as a dental analgesic and antiseptic
modern_information.safety_notes: Clove oil can cause mucosal burns and, if swallowed by children, serious toxicity; it should be used diluted and in small quantities.

exam_points: Lavanga = Syzygium aromaticum (L.) Merr. & L.M.Perry, family Myrtaceae
Rasa Katu, Tikta; Guna Laghu; Virya Sheeta; Vipaka Katu
Karma: Deepana, Pachana, Ruchya, Kaphapittahara, Shoolahara, Kasahara
Indicated in Kasa, Shwasa, Hikka, Chhardi, Trishna, Adhmana
Main constituent: eugenol in clove oil
